metric.external_integration_coverage.formula: score = 100 * confirmed_count / category_total, then adjusted -5 for narrower reliability/breadth signal (single-protocol network stack, no DB/queue integrations) = 90 - 5
metric.external_integration_coverage.limitations: Confirmation is documentation/README-based rather than execution-based; integration 'reliability' (e.g., libcurl timeout/redirect limits, FFmpeg lazy decoder reconstruction, OpenAI structured-output re-validation) is asserted in source docs but not independently load-tested by this worker. The one unconfirmed category (database/other network protocols) is treated as absent rather than assumed present, per the rubric's fail-closed design.

raw_findings.evidence: Language spec defines a narrow explicit C ABI boundary: 'External C declarations remain explicit in the checked program and typed IR' with scalar/void results and explicit string/bin borrow expansion to (pointer, uint64 length) pairs.
`http.get(url)` returns `http.Response | error`; the v0.1 implementation uses libcurl directly, enforces a 5s connect / 30s total timeout, TLS verification, and at most ten redirects.
`json.parse(text)` returns `json.Value | error` with kind/get/at/text/integer/number/boolean/encode/equal methods and duplicate-key/malformed-number rejection.
`image.read`/`image.write` support PNG/JPEG/BMP/TIFF/WebP; README confirms native dependencies 'libpng, libjpeg, libtiff, and libwebp development files (for vision)'.
`video` is described as 'a separate streaming runtime object backed by FFmpeg' with an opaque Reader yielding CPU CHW tensors.

packages.md documents `quidra install owner/repository` and exact `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` git tag resolution; this is independently corroborated by real tagged first-party releases (`quidra-lang/dnn` v0.1.0/v0.2.0, `quidra-lang/vision` v0.1.0/v0.2.0) each declaring `requires.quidra` ranges.

development.md documents a GitHub Actions `release` workflow that tags and publishes releases on push to `main`; a separate pull request in the quidra-lang/quidra repo adds cross-repo CI so 'core changes cannot silently break first-party packages' by continuously testing released vision/dnn packages.

architecture.md: 'The LSP server is a thin client of the ordinary compiler frontend'; README confirms a shipped `quidra lsp` subcommand providing 'compiler-backed diagnostics and formatting over standard LSP stdio framing.'

issue-ai-triage.md documents a GitHub Actions workflow that calls an OpenAI model (default `gpt-5.6-luna`) for issue triage, with Structured Outputs validated locally and a fixed label allowlist as the security boundary.
No database driver, gRPC/WebSocket, or other network-protocol standard module beyond HTTP(S) is documented anywhere in the reviewed specification or README.

rubric.description: Frozen proxy: score = 10 points per confirmed working external-integration category out of a fixed 10-category universe, applied identically across all languages. 'Working' requires a documented, non-trivial implementation surface (not just a stub or aspiration) for that integration.
sources: repo/docs/spec/language.md (http, json, image, video, C FFI sections)
repo/docs/spec/architecture.md (C FFI boundary, native runtime boundary)

metric.implemented_platform_coverage.limitations: Platform confirmation relies on documentation/README/CI descriptions rather than direct execution of the release pipeline; packaging detail (Linux DEB/TGZ, macOS TGZ, Windows ZIP via CPack, per README search snippet) corroborates 3 desktop OS artifacts but ARM64/mobile targets are not evidenced and are scored as absent rather than assumed present.

raw_findings.evidence: Release checks require 'GCC and Clang release builds' and 'Linux, macOS, and Windows CI'; native runtime boundary documents libquidra_runtime.a for Unix-like hosts and /proc/self/exe self-location on Linux.
Same CI line covers macOS; native runtime boundary documents Mach-O executable-path API self-location and Metal compute path is macOS/Apple Silicon specific.

Same CI line covers Windows; native runtime boundary documents quidra_runtime.lib and GetModuleFileNameW self-location; GitHub README build instructions show a distinct Windows/PowerShell/vcpkg/CMake -A x64 build path.
No architecture-specific (ARM64) Linux target is named in the docs or README beyond WSL/NVIDIA driver interop notes; only generic 'Linux' CI is described.
Architecture doc states explicitly: 'Apple Silicon uses `metal`', tying a concrete GPU backend to that specific architecture/target.

Architecture doc describes a dedicated 'WebAssembly frontend boundary' with QUIDRA_BUILD_WASM_FRONTEND building quidra_core plus wasm_api.cpp and a versioned quidra_wasm_invoke entry point; the quidra-lang/playground repo independently confirms a shipped product described as 'the real Quidra compiler frontend, compiled to WebAssembly and running in your browser tab.'
Architecture doc: on Linux/Windows NVIDIA the runtime dynamically loads the NVIDIA Driver API, with canonical backend id `cuda`.
Architecture doc: 'On AMD, Quidra dynamically uses the HIP runtime and HIP runtime compilation facilities when a compatible ROCm/HIP installation is present', canonical backend id `hip`.
Architecture doc: 'On macOS, allocation, copies and compute use Metal', canonical backend id `metal`, with explicit note that Metal lacks FP64 compute.
No mobile OS target, cross-compilation path, or mobile packaging is described anywhere in the docs, README, or CI job list.

rubric.description: Frozen proxy: score = 10 points per confirmed-implemented platform/target category out of a fixed 10-category universe, applied identically across all languages in this evaluation. Evidence must show the category is actually implemented/shipped by the evaluated toolchain (build target, CI job, or runtime backend), not merely aspirational roadmap text.
sources: repo/docs/spec/architecture.md (Runtime representation and lifetime policy; Native runtime boundary)
